briefing.localWatch: The $6.8 billion South Coast rail electrification commitment is the central local story, with Shoalhaven campaigners quoted by the South Coast Register saying delivery is the real test. Nothing else in today's supplied coverage bears directly on Kiama or the South Coast.

stories.headline: Rail announcement gives the region real hope for the future says campaigner
stories.summary: The South Coast Register reports Premier Chris Minns has promised $6.8 billion to electrify South Coast rail lines, following what the paper describes as a 10-year union push. Campaigners quoted by the paper welcomed the announcement but said delivery would be the real test.

stories.headline: No safe seats in the Hunter this election: NSW Premier Chris Minns
stories.summary: The Newcastle Herald reports Premier Chris Minns has acknowledged that One Nation is tied with Labor at 32 per cent in the Hunter, and says no seat in the region can be considered safe. The paper reports on how the government intends to fight back in the region.

stories.headline: Former NSW Liberal leads overhaul of One Nation candidate selection process
stories.summary: In an exclusive, The Guardian reports that Mark Jones, who it says was once on track for one of the Liberal Party's most powerful roles, is now instrumental in One Nation's expansion and is leading a rework of how the party selects candidates.

stories.headline: Libs face election fight with just $200
stories.summary: The Australian reports the NSW Liberals are heading into the election contest with just $200 available to them. No further detail was available in the supplied text.

stories.headline: Some NSW police are now armed with military-style rifles. And they could be deployed to protests
stories.summary: The Guardian reports NSW Police on Sunday launched a permanent special unit, described as an Australian first, to patrol tourist areas, crowded public spaces, major events, sporting matches and places of worship while carrying military rifles. The paper reports Jewish groups have welcomed the new patrol unit following the Bondi terror attack, while experts it spoke to say police use of long-arm firearms must be strictly controlled.

stories.headline: Mammoth cost of post-Bondi policing revealed
stories.summary: The Sydney Morning Herald reports on the cost of the expanded NSW Police presence put in place after the Bondi terror attack, with officers deployed at places of worship, schools and community hubs.

stories.headline: From homework to big kids: What keeps primary school students up at night
stories.summary: The Sydney Morning Herald reports the NSW government is investing in mental fitness programs in schools as childhood anxiety rates climb.

stories.headline: Housing must be delivered with, not before, key infrastructure
stories.summary: In the Sydney Morning Herald, the argument is put that housing and infrastructure need to be delivered together rather than housing arriving first. The piece notes Productivity Commissioner Peter Achterstraat has long made that case.

elsewhere.text: Federal housing politics: the Milton Ulladulla Times reports a Liberal MP has signalled the party might back away from a fight over whether home-buyers should be able to use superannuation.
The Guardian reports discontent in Anthony Albanese's inner-west Sydney seat of Grayndler, home to more than 3,000 cultural and creative businesses, over a federal proposal on AI and copyright.
